title: Fix custom-command rewrite keeps OpenCode frontmatter
description: Live case 2 showed with_skill correctly audited agent/model as non-portable but kept them in the rewritten shared command. Strengthen skill instructions so shared rewrites remove behavior-changing OpenCode frontmatter, then validate with tests and case-2 live eval if practical.
notes: CURRENT: GREEN and live-validated. Added failing unit assertion that custom-command skill must remove agent/model/subtask from emitted frontmatter when rewriting an existing agent-specific command into one shared file. Updated SKILL.md to say not to merely audit and keep those fields; use a separate OpenCode-specific variant if preserving them. VALIDATION: python3 -m unittest tests.test_skill_eval -v (23 tests). LIVE CASE 2 VALIDATION: SKILL_EVAL_ALLOW_LIVE_PI=1 python3 -m tools.skill_eval /tmp/custom-command-live-case2-fix.EKn7sz/manifest.case2.json workflow --results /tmp/custom-command-live-case2-fix.EKn7sz/results --require-real; both with_skill and without_skill passed this run, with_skill 10/10 checks.

title: Improve custom-command real eval reliability
description: Implement follow-up recommendations from live custom-command eval analysis: artifact-aware grading, robust markdown extraction, process-failure vs grade-failure separation, clarified eval prompt contract, and strengthened custom-command skill output instructions.
notes: CURRENT: GREEN. Implemented all 5 live-eval recommendations. 1) custom-command grader is artifact-aware via sandbox_path/artifact_manifest context and prefers generated .md artifacts. 2) Markdown extraction handles text fences, md/markdown fences, four-backtick outer fences, nested triple fences, and recommended filename text fences. 3) runner marks timeout/nonzero process outcomes as process_failed and writes grade.status=not_graded with passed=null instead of content failures. 4) eval prompts explicitly allow returning command content or writing files and require summarizing written paths/install paths. 5) custom-command skill now says to return full content unless asked to write/install and to use a four-backtick outer fence for nested fences. VALIDATION: python3 -m unittest tests.test_skill_eval -v (23 tests); python3 -m tools.skill_eval skills/custom-command/evals/manifest.json workflow --results /tmp/custom-command-real-validation2.49iY0Q --require-real (10 honest skipped runs with live Pi disabled).
close_reason: Implemented artifact-aware grading, robust Markdown extraction, process-failure separation, clarified eval prompt contract, and strengthened skill instructions with TDD coverage.

title: Document and validate proper skill eval workflow
description:
## What to build

Document how maintainers run proper skill evals, interpret results, and avoid confusing smoke tests with behavioral benchmarks.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Documentation explains manifest suites, harness modes, with/without-skill comparison, grading, traces, and regression promotion.
- [ ] Example commands show smoke/static runs and real harness runs separately.
- [ ] Validation command or test suite verifies the documented custom-command real eval path using fake harness tests where live credentials are unavailable.
- [ ] Maintainer guidance states when a result is trustworthy enough to compare skill versions.

## Notes

Close this after the real-eval workflow is usable by another agent without rediscovering caveats from context.
notes: CURRENT: GREEN. Added docs/skill-evals.md covering manifest suites, harness modes, with_skill/without_skill, static smoke vs real Pi commands, --require-real, SKILL_EVAL_ALLOW_LIVE_PI=1, grading, trace artifacts, metric interpretation, regression promotion, trust criteria, and validation commands. VALIDATION: python3 -m unittest tests.test_skill_eval -v; python3 -m tools.skill_eval skills/custom-command/evals/manifest.json workflow --results /tmp/custom-command-real-validation.ckEnMM --require-real (10 honest skipped runs with live Pi disabled).
close_reason: Documented and validated proper skill eval workflow with tests and CLI validation.

title: Promote real eval failures into regression suite cases
description:
## What to build

Add a workflow for converting observed real harness failures into regression suite cases linked to the source failure and trace artifacts.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Regression cases can reference source run IDs, trace paths, and failure summaries.
- [ ] A helper command or documented CLI flow creates regression cases from failed runs.
- [ ] Regression suites remain separate from workflow/capability suites.
- [ ] Created follow-up beads link back to the source review or failure bead.
- [ ] Tests cover regression metadata serialization and loader behavior.

## Notes

Every real failure should become a future regression eval before the skill is edited.
notes: CURRENT: GREEN. Added tools.skill_eval.regression.promote_failures_to_regression_cases and CLI helper 'python3 -m tools.skill_eval promote-regressions <manifest> --results <dir> --output <manifest> --source-bead <id>'. It promotes failed non-skipped real harness runs into a separate regression suite with source_run_id, trace_path, failure_summary, source suite/case/config, harness mode, and source_bead metadata. Loader preserves promoted metadata. VALIDATION: python3 -m unittest tests.test_skill_eval -v. NEXT: agents-1cs.8 documentation and validation workflow.
close_reason: Implemented real failure promotion into regression suite cases with helper CLI and tests.

title: Report real-vs-synthetic metrics and benchmark caveats
description:
## What to build

Update benchmark.json and report.md so readers can tell whether pass rates, timings, usage, and token metrics came from real agent runs, replayed runs, or synthetic smoke tests.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] benchmark.json includes harness mode, synthetic flag, model/provider, and metric provenance per configuration.
- [ ] report.md shows a clear warning for synthetic or replayed results.
- [ ] Real timings and usage are separated from synthetic character-count placeholders.
- [ ] Token fields are populated when available and null/unknown is explained when not available.
- [ ] Comparison deltas are hidden or caveated when modes are not comparable.

## Notes

This addresses the agents-bf0.8 review concern that current reports can overstate synthetic result meaning.
notes: CURRENT: GREEN. benchmark.json now carries harness_mode, synthetic flag, model/provider, and metric_provenance per configuration; report.md warns for synthetic/replay, explains unknown token metrics vs character counts, shows provenance, and caveats comparisons when synthetic or modes differ while preserving deltas for inspection. VALIDATION: python3 -m unittest tests.test_skill_eval -v. NEXT: agents-1cs.7 promote real eval failures into regression suite cases.
close_reason: Reported real-vs-synthetic metric provenance and benchmark caveats with tests.

title: Capture real trace, artifact, and workspace evidence
description:
## What to build

Expand real harness trace bundles so reviewers can debug process failures and output artifacts after a run.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Trace bundle records normalized agent/tool/session events when available.
- [ ] Workspace diff or artifact manifest is captured for evals that write files.
- [ ] Raw harness/session data is preserved for future process graders.
- [ ] metadata.json records harness mode, sandbox path, skill paths loaded, model/provider, and eval manifest version.
- [ ] Tests cover trace bundle presence and schema shape using fake harness data.

## Notes

The goal is post-run explainability, not a full UI rewrite.
notes: CURRENT: GREEN. Each run now writes artifact_manifest.json and workspace_diff.txt from sandbox before/after snapshots, keeps raw_output/session/process data, normalized events, and richer metadata with manifest version/path, suite, case, configuration, sandbox, harness mode/model/provider, and loaded skill paths. VALIDATION: python3 -m unittest tests.test_skill_eval -v. NEXT: agents-1cs.6 report real-vs-synthetic metrics and caveats.
close_reason: Captured real trace, artifact, workspace diff, and richer metadata evidence with tests.

title: Replace custom-command legacy expectation prose with structured checks
description:
## What to build

Convert custom-command eval expectations from literal prose matching into structured deterministic checks that evaluate generated command artifacts and compatibility behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Checks verify filename shape, Markdown fence/content, YAML frontmatter, description field, `$ARGUMENTS`, and install paths where applicable.
- [ ] Checks reject behavior-changing frontmatter such as agent/model/subtask when portability requires identical behavior.
- [ ] Checks reject required OpenCode shell injection and required @file inclusion in shared commands.
- [ ] Checks can inspect extracted Markdown command blocks rather than only raw response text.
- [ ] Legacy expectation prose remains as human rubric/context, not as required literal output.

## Notes

This makes real generated outputs gradeable without requiring exact wording.
notes: CURRENT: GREEN. Added suite custom_grader support, non_empty_response deterministic check, custom-command structured grader checks for filename, markdown command fence/frontmatter/description, , disallowed agent/model/subtask frontmatter, shell injection, @file inclusion, positional slicing, and install paths for case 1. Legacy expectation prose remains in cases as human rubric/context but is no longer converted into required literal checks because migrated cases declare structured checks. VALIDATION: python3 -m unittest tests.test_skill_eval -v. NEXT: agents-1cs.5 real trace/artifact/workspace evidence.
close_reason: Replaced custom-command literal legacy grading with structured deterministic checks and custom grader coverage.

title: Run custom-command workflow suite with real generated outputs
description:
## What to build

Switch the custom-command workflow benchmark path from static responses to the real Pi harness for both with_skill and without_skill configurations.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] custom-command workflow suite can run all existing cases through the real harness.
- [ ] with_skill force-loads the custom-command skill.
- [ ] without_skill runs the same prompts without the custom-command skill.
- [ ] response.md contains actual generated agent output, not expected_output or prompt echoes.
- [ ] The runner records unsupported/skipped status when live harness prerequisites are missing instead of faking results.

## Notes

This is the first proper behavioral benchmark slice.
notes: CURRENT: GREEN. custom-command workflow manifest now defaults to real pi harness for with_skill/without_skill. Live Pi execution is gated, so default local runs skip honestly instead of emitting expected/prompt text. Static smoke remains available through explicit configurations. Fake-pi test proves all 5 cases x 2 configs can run as non-synthetic real harness outputs. VALIDATION: python3 -m unittest tests.test_skill_eval -v. NEXT: agents-1cs.4 structured custom-command grading.
close_reason: Switched custom-command workflow default to real Pi harness with skipped-prerequisite behavior and fake real-harness coverage.

title: Implement real Pi workflow harness adapter
description:
## What to build

Add a real workflow harness adapter that invokes Pi non-interactively in an isolated sandbox and returns generated response text plus raw session/process artifacts.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Harness can execute one eval prompt through `pi --print` or equivalent non-interactive mode.
- [ ] Harness supports with_skill by force-loading the target skill.
- [ ] Harness supports without_skill by disabling skill loading or omitting the target skill.
- [ ] Raw stdout/stderr, exit status, session metadata, timing, and configured model/provider are captured.
- [ ] Tests use a fake Pi executable or adapter seam so CI does not require API keys.

## Notes

Keep external network/model execution behind explicit configuration; unit tests should validate adapter behavior without calling a live LLM.
notes: CURRENT: GREEN. Added real Pi harness adapter using non-interactive pi -p, isolated sandbox cwd, explicit --no-* resource flags, with_skill via --skill and without_skill via --no-skills, stdout/stderr/exit/command capture, model/provider metadata, and fake executable test seam. Live execution gated by allow_live or SKILL_EVAL_ALLOW_LIVE_PI=1. VALIDATION: python3 -m unittest tests.test_skill_eval -v. NEXT: agents-1cs.3 switch custom-command workflow config to real harness with skipped prerequisites instead of fake static output.
close_reason: Implemented real Pi workflow harness adapter with fake-executable TDD coverage.

title: Define real harness contract and static-harness boundaries
description:
## What to build

Define the runner contract for real agent execution and explicitly demote the current static harness to smoke-test-only usage.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Harness result schema distinguishes static, replay, and real agent execution modes.
- [ ] Static harness outputs are labeled synthetic in summary, benchmark, report, and trace metadata.
- [ ] Runner configuration can reject synthetic harnesses for benchmark-quality runs.
- [ ] Tests cover synthetic labeling and real-harness-required validation.

## Notes

Start here so later tasks do not accidentally treat synthetic pass rates as behavioral quality signals.
notes: CURRENT: GREEN. Added harness contract metadata distinguishing static/replay/real modes; static/replay marked synthetic in run metadata, raw output, summary, benchmark config summaries, and report warning. run_suite(require_real=True) rejects synthetic configs. VALIDATION: python3 -m unittest tests.test_skill_eval -v. NEXT: agents-1cs.2 real Pi workflow adapter.
close_reason: Implemented harness mode contract, synthetic labeling, report caveat, and require_real validation with tests.

title: Epic: Real behavioral skill eval framework
description:
## Source

Created from HITL review of agents-bf0.8 after the first synthetic custom-command eval vertical slice.

## Problem

The current skill eval framework proves the plumbing for manifests, trace bundles, deterministic grading, and reports, but the custom-command benchmark is synthetic: with_skill emits expected text and without_skill emits prompts. Pass rates, timing, and usage are schema smoke signals rather than trustworthy behavioral measurements.

## Goal

Move the framework from synthetic/static testing to proper behavior testing by running real agent harness executions, grading generated artifacts with structured deterministic checks, capturing real traces/usage, and promoting observed failures into regression suites.

## Definition of done

- Static harness remains available only for smoke tests and is clearly labeled.
- A real workflow harness can run custom-command cases with and without the skill.
- Reports make it clear whether metrics are synthetic or real.
- custom-command grading checks generated command content and compatibility contracts, not literal expectation prose.
- Real failures can be promoted into regression cases.
close_reason: Completed real behavioral skill eval framework epic with TDD: real Pi harness adapter, real custom-command workflow configs, structured grading, trace/artifact evidence, metric caveats, regression promotion helper, and workflow documentation all validated.

title: PRD: Skill Eval Framework Vertical Slice
description:
## Problem Statement

Skill evaluation in this repository is currently useful but fragmented. Some skills have hand-built evals and workspaces, while most skills have none. Existing results are difficult to reproduce, compare, or trust because runners, schemas, traces, grading methods, and benchmark formats vary across experiments.

The user wants skill evals to behave like end-to-end regression tests for agent behavior, not just output snapshots. A good framework should verify whether a skill triggers, whether the agent follows the intended process, whether outputs meet contracts, whether bundled resources are used appropriately, and whether the skill justifies its time/token overhead.

## Solution

Build a central skill evaluation framework with a minimal end-to-end vertical slice using the `custom-command` skill as the first target. The framework will provide shared runner behavior, standardized result schemas, trace capture, deterministic grading, and with/without-skill comparison while keeping skill-specific eval data, fixtures, rubrics, and optional custom checks local to each skill.

The first version will prioritize a working workflow-eval slice over full framework completeness. It will run existing `custom-command` eval cases in isolated sandboxes, capture trace bundles and final responses, grade deterministic output contracts, compare `with_skill` against `without_skill`, and produce durable results that can later support trigger evals, regression suites, LLM judges, and richer fixtures.

## User Stories

1. As a skill maintainer, I want one central runner for skill evals, so that every skill is evaluated consistently.
2. As a skill maintainer, I want each skill to own its own eval datasets and fixtures, so that skill-specific behavior stays close to the skill.
3. As a skill maintainer, I want to run a small golden prompt set, so that I can catch behavior regressions before changing or publishing a skill.
4. As a skill maintainer, I want workflow evals to force-load a skill when appropriate, so that I can test whether the skill helps once loaded.
5. As a skill maintainer, I want trigger evals to be modeled separately from workflow evals, so that I do not confuse instruction-following with natural skill invocation.
6. As a skill maintainer, I want eval runs isolated in clean sandboxes, so that results are not affected by previous runs or dirty workspace state.
7. As a skill maintainer, I want each run to save raw and normalized traces, so that I can inspect agent behavior after the run completes.
8. As a skill maintainer, I want deterministic checks for objective expectations, so that simple failures are graded cheaply and reliably.
9. As a skill maintainer, I want optional custom deterministic graders, so that domain-specific output contracts can be checked precisely.
10. As a skill maintainer, I want LLM judges available only for subjective checks, so that nuanced quality can be assessed without making every eval expensive or flaky.
11. As a skill maintainer, I want to compare `with_skill` against `without_skill`, so that I can see whether a skill justifies its overhead.
12. As a skill maintainer, I want to compare current results against previous versions later, so that regressions are visible during skill edits.
13. As a skill maintainer, I want result metrics for pass rate, time, tokens, errors, and deltas, so that quality and efficiency are evaluated together.
14. As a skill maintainer, I want eval suites separated by purpose, so that capability work and regression safety do not get mixed together.
15. As a skill maintainer, I want existing eval files to be usable during migration, so that current work is not thrown away.
16. As a skill maintainer, I want the first vertical slice to use a deterministic, dependency-light skill, so that framework problems are not hidden behind external service failures.
17. As a skill maintainer, I want every real skill failure to become a future regression eval, so that the eval suite compounds over time.
18. As a skill maintainer, I want result data stored in language-neutral schemas, so that the runner can be rewritten or wrapped later without losing historical compatibility.

## Implementation Decisions

- The framework will use a central repo-level runner rather than per-skill custom runners as the default architecture.
- Skill-specific eval data will remain local to each skill, including datasets, fixtures, rubrics, and optional custom deterministic checks.
- The first implementation will be a minimal vertical slice rather than a complete framework rewrite.
- The first target skill will be `custom-command` because it has existing eval cases, deterministic output contracts, no external service dependency, and useful with/without-skill contrast.
- The canonical framework code will live as repo-level tooling, while the skill-authoring guidance will document or wrap that tooling rather than owning it.
- The framework will distinguish forced workflow evals from real trigger evals.
- The first vertical slice may implement forced workflow mode first, but trigger mode will remain first-class in the schemas and design.
- Each run will save a trace bundle containing raw harness output, normalized events, final response/artifacts, timing/usage, workspace diff where applicable, and grading results.
- Normalized traces may start minimal in the vertical slice, but raw trace data will be preserved so future process graders can extract additional signals without rerunning historical evals.
- Deterministic grading will be layered: generic declarative checks first, with optional skill-local custom checks for domain-specific validation.
- LLM judging will be modeled as an optional fallback for subjective checks, not as the default grading mechanism.
- The first `custom-command` slice can run entirely deterministically if no subjective checks require a judge.
- All eval runs will go through a fixture-aware sandbox interface.
- The first slice will use a trivial empty fixture while preserving the abstraction needed for full fixture-copy support later.
- The comparison model will support arbitrary named configurations.
- The first vertical slice will compare `with_skill` against `without_skill`.
- Eval datasets will be organized through a suite-aware manifest.
- Existing eval data can initially be mapped as a workflow suite to avoid unnecessary migration friction.
- Future suites will include trigger, negative, capability, and regression cases.
- The first implementation will be in Python to reuse existing repo eval infrastructure quickly.
- Eval cases, traces, grades, and benchmark data will use language-neutral JSON or JSONL schemas so that a future TypeScript runner or wrapper remains possible.

## Testing Decisions

- Tests should verify external behavior and stable contracts, not incidental implementation details.
- The manifest loader should be tested for suite resolution, skill metadata handling, and compatibility with existing eval definitions.
- The sandbox manager should be tested for isolated workspaces and repeatable empty-fixture behavior.
- The runner should be tested for named configuration execution and correct result organization.
- The trace capture layer should be tested for producing the expected trace bundle shape, including raw output, normalized events, response artifacts, timing/usage, and grading output.
- The deterministic grader should be tested with generic checks such as required content, forbidden content, regex checks, and structured output checks.
- Skill-local custom grading should be supported by interface-level tests, even if the first slice uses only simple custom logic.
- The comparison layer should be tested for pass-rate delta, timing delta, token delta, and per-case result aggregation.
- The first end-to-end test should run the `custom-command` workflow suite through both `with_skill` and `without_skill` configurations and produce comparable results.
- LLM judge support should be represented in schemas and control flow, but not required for the first deterministic `custom-command` slice.
- Trigger eval execution should be deferred if necessary, but trigger suite representation should be covered by schema or loader tests.

## Out of Scope

- Full multi-harness support across every supported agent environment in the first vertical slice.
- Full fixture-copy and repository-reset support beyond the initial fixture-aware empty sandbox.
- Comprehensive trigger eval execution for every skill.
- Converting every skill in the repository to the new eval format.
- Rewriting all existing review and benchmark UI surfaces.
- Making LLM judges mandatory.
- Evaluating external-service-heavy skills such as browser or web-scraping skills in the first slice.
- Building a polished TypeScript CLI before the Python vertical slice proves the framework shape.

## Further Notes

The framework should treat real failures as future regression cases. When a skill misses invocation, uses the wrong process, ignores a reference, produces a bad artifact, or wastes excessive tools/tokens, that scenario should be captured as an eval before the skill is changed.

The long-term goal is a compounding regression system for agent skills: small golden prompt sets, clean sandboxes, trace-based process checks, deterministic-first grading, optional subjective judging, and comparable old/new or with/without results.
